open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: On every call MUST read the configuration file's bytes, opening config_path as read_configuration does
open_points.question: Which configuration path must current_token_list use, given that it has no config_path parameter, and what happens if it is called before load_installation establishes one?
options: Use the path from the first successful load_installation call and raise before initialization
Use the path from the first successful load_installation call and return None before initialization
Use some externally implied default path
open_points.default_guess: Store the path from the first successful load_installation call and return None before initialization.

open_points.subject: load_installation
open_points.text: MUST call read_configuration once at start, keep the returned Installation for the life of the process
open_points.question: What must happen on a second or concurrent call to load_installation, especially when it supplies a different config_path?
options: Return the first loaded Installation without reading again
Reload and replace the retained Installation
Raise an initialization error
Call read_configuration once per invocation
open_points.default_guess: Initialize once and thereafter return the first retained Installation, ignoring later paths.

open_points.subject: load_installation
open_points.text: MUST call read_configuration once at start, keep the returned Installation for the life of the process, and keep the SHA-256 of the file's bytes as the last read digest
open_points.question: How is load_installation to obtain the digest of the exact bytes validated by read_configuration when read_configuration returns only Installation?
options: Have read_configuration record hidden digest state
Reopen and reread the path after read_configuration, risking different bytes
Use a private shared reader whose extra result is indirectly exposed to load_installation
open_points.default_guess: Use a private shared reader and have read_configuration record the digest of the same opened file for load_installation to consume.

open_points.subject: load_installation
open_points.text: a failed check propagates InstallationRejectedError and nothing is kept
open_points.question: If initialization has already succeeded and a later load_installation call fails, does 'nothing is kept' discard the previously retained installation or leave it intact?
options: Discard all retained state
Keep the original process-lifetime installation
Disallow later loading before performing checks
open_points.default_guess: Disallow reloading and keep the original installation.

open_points.subject: module retained state
open_points.text: keep the returned Installation for the life of the process, and keep the SHA-256 ... as the last read digest and ... as the current token list
open_points.question: What synchronization and observable behavior are required when load_installation and current_token_list are called concurrently?
options: Serialize initialization and token refresh with a lock
Permit races under ordinary module globals
Assume the functions are never called concurrently
open_points.default_guess: Protect retained state and refreshes with a module-level lock.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: opening config_path as read_configuration does, component by component without following a symbolic link at any component ... and applies exactly four checks
open_points.question: Does a token refresh repeat read_configuration's regular-file, effective-owner, and private-permission checks, or does 'exactly four checks' mean that only safe path opening, parsing, and token checks apply?
options: Repeat all filesystem security checks before the four token checks
Only prohibit symlink traversal and require readable bytes
Treat any metadata change as a failed token refresh
open_points.default_guess: Only prohibit symlink traversal and require readable bytes, because the refresh explicitly specifies exactly four checks.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: parses as a JSON object with owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types
open_points.question: Must the refreshed JSON still contain exactly every Installation field with valid types, or are only owner_token and agent_tokens parsed and all other members ignored?
options: Validate the complete Installation schema
Require and validate only owner_token and agent_tokens while ignoring other members
Require all Installation members but validate only the token members
open_points.default_guess: Require and validate only owner_token and agent_tokens, ignoring other members.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types
open_points.question: Must each refreshed agent-token object have exactly the three AgentToken fields, or may it contain additional members?
options: Require exactly agent_name, token, and may_author
Allow additional members and ignore them
Delegate to whatever coercion and extra-field policy the imported model implements
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly the declared AgentToken fields.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file ... the new digest becomes the last read digest
open_points.question: When the comparison read and validation reread produce different bytes, which bytes are validated and which digest is retained?
options: Validate the second read and retain its digest
Validate the first read and retain its digest
Retry until two consecutive reads match
Treat the change between reads as failure
open_points.default_guess: Validate the second read and retain the digest of that second read.

open_points.subject: current_token_list
open_points.text: when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file ... when the file cannot be read the last read digest is cleared
open_points.question: If the first read fails but the required reread succeeds, is the successful reread accepted, and if the first succeeds but the reread fails, must the digest be cleared and the token list discarded?
options: Use the reread outcome in both cases
Any failure during either read makes the refresh fail
Use the first read whenever it succeeded
open_points.default_guess: Use the reread outcome: accept a successful reread, but clear the digest and list if the reread fails.

open_points.question: Which failures count as a 'bad file' and must be suppressed—only validation and expected filesystem errors, or every exception arising during refresh, including model-construction and hashing errors?
options: Suppress expected open/read/parse/schema/validation errors only
Suppress every exception and return None
Suppress only InstallationRejectedError
open_points.default_guess: Suppress expected filesystem, JSON, schema, and token-validation failures, but not unrelated programming or resource errors.

open_points.subject: manifest_source
open_points.text: MUST return ManifestSource with manifest_location and manifest_revision of the Installation loaded at start
open_points.question: What happens if manifest_source is called before a successful load_installation?
options: Raise a defined module-local exception
Raise a generic runtime error
Return a sentinel or empty ManifestSource
Assume this call order cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Raise RuntimeError indicating that installation has not been loaded.

open_points.subject: selected_instance_name

open_points.question: What happens if selected_instance_name is called before a successful load_installation?
options: Raise an initialization error
Return None
Assume this call order cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Raise RuntimeError indicating that installation has not been loaded.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential

open_points.question: What happens if resolve_service_credential is called before a successful load_installation?
options: Raise CredentialUnresolvedError
Raise an initialization error
Treat it as no credential configured
open_points.default_guess: Raise CredentialUnresolvedError naming the requested service and unavailable installation state.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: MUST raise InstallationRejectedError naming the first failing check
open_points.question: What exact exception message or argument structure is required to 'name' a failing check?
options: Use fixed human-readable messages
Use stable symbolic check names
Include the config path and operating-system detail
Pass structured data in exception arguments
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed human-readable messages identifying the check without exposing unnecessary filesystem details.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: MUST raise CredentialUnresolvedError, whose reason names the service and the failing check
open_points.question: What exact reason format and exception arguments are required, and may safe path or OS-error details be included?
options: Use a fixed message containing service_id and a symbolic check name
Include safe OS-error details and the path
Use multiple exception arguments for service and check
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed message containing repr(service_id) and a generic failing-check description, with no secret content.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object
open_points.question: Which byte encodings and JSON parser extensions are accepted?
options: Require UTF-8 JSON only
Use the standard json bytes behavior, which can detect UTF-16/UTF-32
Decode with UTF-8-sig and allow a BOM
open_points.default_guess: Require UTF-8 JSON, allowing only behavior explicitly accepted by Python's strict JSON decoder after UTF-8 decoding.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: one JSON object whose members are exactly the fields of Installation
open_points.question: Are duplicate JSON member names rejected, or may the JSON parser keep one occurrence and then validate the resulting mapping?
options: Reject every duplicate member name
Use the last occurrence as standard json.loads does
Use the first occurrence
open_points.default_guess: Reject duplicate JSON member names.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: whose members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types
open_points.question: Must JSON values match the declared Python types strictly, or may imported model validation coerce values such as integers to strings, lists to tuples, or truthy values to booleans?
options: Perform strict JSON-type validation before constructing models
Use the imported models' default validation and coercion
Use model validation in explicit strict mode
open_points.default_guess: Validate strictly, while converting JSON arrays to the declared tuple fields.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: members are exactly the fields of Installation with their types
open_points.question: Does 'exactly' also require every nested service and agent object to contain exactly its declared fields and no extras?
options: Apply exact-member validation recursively
Apply exactness only to the top-level Installation object
Delegate nested extra-field handling to imported models
open_points.default_guess: Apply exact-member validation recursively.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: a service appears twice in service_instances or in service_credentials
open_points.question: If both collections contain duplicates, which duplicate check fails first, and are the collections scanned completely in the written collection order?
options: Check all service_instances before all service_credentials
Traverse both collections together
Report whichever duplicate occurs at the lowest element index
open_points.default_guess: Check service_instances in tuple order, then service_credentials in tuple order.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: a credential header name is not an HTTP field-name token ...; a credential's secret_file is not an absolute path
open_points.question: Are all header names checked before any secret_file path, as the listed check order implies, or are both properties checked credential by credential?
options: Check every header name first, then every secret_file
For each credential, check its header then its path
Report the earliest failing credential regardless of failure kind
open_points.default_guess: Check all header names first, then all secret_file paths, preserving the stated check order.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component
open_points.question: How must relative paths, '.', '..', repeated separators, a trailing separator, and changes to the working directory during traversal be handled?
options: Accept relative paths and resolve them from a captured starting-directory descriptor
Normalize lexical components before opening
Reject '.', '..', empty, and trailing components
Require an absolute config_path
open_points.default_guess: Accept absolute or relative paths, traverse from a captured root or current-directory descriptor, ignore '.' and repeated separators, and resolve '..' without following symlinks.

open_points.subject: read_configuration and resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: component by component without following a symbolic link at any component
open_points.question: Must directory descriptors remain open throughout traversal to prevent component-replacement races, and how are platforms lacking descriptor-relative no-follow operations handled?
options: Use descriptor-relative traversal and fail when the platform cannot guarantee it
Use lstat followed by ordinary open
Assume a POSIX platform with the needed flags
open_points.default_guess: Assume POSIX and use descriptor-relative opens with no-follow flags while retaining parent descriptors as needed.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: is not owned by the process's effective user
open_points.question: Is ownership compared only with the effective UID at the time of the file check, and what behavior is required on platforms without effective-UID ownership semantics?
options: Compare st_uid with os.geteuid and fail if unavailable
Use the real UID
Treat ownership as satisfied on non-POSIX platforms
open_points.default_guess: Compare the opened file's st_uid with os.geteuid and reject if the check cannot be performed.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: every token is at least the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant long
open_points.question: Is token length measured in Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes, or another unit?
options: Python string length in Unicode code points
UTF-8 encoded byte length
ASCII characters only, rejecting non-ASCII tokens
open_points.default_guess: Measure Python string length in Unicode code points.

open_points.subject: read_configuration
open_points.text: the bytes cannot be read or do not parse as one JSON object
open_points.question: Is there any maximum configuration-file size or bounded-read requirement?
options: Read the entire file without a stated limit
Apply RELEASE_CEILING_BOUNDED_TEXT_BYTES_MAX
Introduce a separate implementation-defined safety limit
open_points.default_guess: Read the entire file because no configuration-size limit is specified.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: when no credential is configured for service_id or the secret file is missing, unreadable, not private, larger ... or not valid UTF-8, or its value is empty or holds a control character
open_points.question: What is the required first-failure order among file type, ownership, permissions, size, read errors, UTF-8 decoding, emptiness, and control characters?
options: Use the order implied by BEHAVIOR followed by the VALIDATION_ERROR list
Use the exact order of the VALIDATION_ERROR list
Report whichever operating-system operation fails first
open_points.default_guess: Check safe opening, regular-file status, owner, permissions, bounded size/read, UTF-8, newline removal, emptiness, then control characters.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: the checks and the read using that one opened file, which must be a regular file, owned by the process's effective user
open_points.question: Which named failing check should be reported when the secret path opens successfully but is not a regular file or is owned by another user, since the failure list names only missing, unreadable, and not private?
options: Classify both as not private
Classify both as unreadable
Give each a distinct failing-check reason
open_points.default_guess: Give non-regular and wrong-owner files distinct failing-check reasons.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: decoded as UTF-8 with exactly one trailing newline removed when present
open_points.question: Does 'newline' mean only a final LF character, a final CRLF pair, or any Unicode line-ending sequence?
options: Remove one final LF only
Remove one final CRLF pair or one LF
Use splitlines semantics for any Unicode line ending
open_points.default_guess: Remove one final LF only; a preceding CR remains and is rejected as a control character.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential
open_points.text: its value is empty or holds a control character
open_points.question: Which characters count as control characters?
options: ASCII C0 controls plus DEL
Every Unicode character in general category Cc
All Unicode categories beginning with C
HTTP-invalid header-value characters
open_points.default_guess: Reject every Unicode category Cc character.

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential

Use stat size first and bounded reading only when needed
Require stat size and bytes read to agree

open_points.subject: resolve_service_credential

open_points.question: Is emptiness tested after removing the one trailing newline, making a file containing only that newline invalid?

Test before newline removal
Reject whitespace-only values as empty
open_points.default_guess: Test after newline removal, so a lone newline is invalid while other whitespace is not empty.
